answer: Seats are sold in a per-epoch auction open only to holders of a hardware-rooted attestation bound to one verified person. One person holds one seat, so a thousand keys buy nothing; fielding N agents needs N real attestations, each with separate legal exposure. The falcon is the auctioneer enforcing that cap: bidders race a price ladder, so marginal seats get costly fast. Each bid posts a sable stake, forfeited if audit finds a rented or spoofed attestation, and the reputation trellis of past rounds exposes rental clusters sharing one funding source. Cost scales linearly with attacker size.
